text: Fiona the hippo dies after eating a hat at Cincinnati Zoo. ## In short: Fiona the hippo has died after swallowing a hat that accidentally ended up in her enclosure at Cincinnati Zoo. The nine-year-old hippopotamus has had a global following since her premature birth in 2017. Cincinnati Zoo is where Harambe the gorilla was killed after a child got into his enclosure a decade ago. Fiona the hippo, whose premature birth and fight for survival at Cincinnati Zoo captured global attention in 2017, has died after eating a woolly hat. The hippopotamus had been under 24-hour medical care for about 11 days after ingesting the hat. A child had thrown the knitted cap into the air when a ceiling fan caught and flung it through a small opening above Fiona's enclosure. Cincinnati Zoo said in a statement that "vet staff tried everything they could to help" Fiona. "Despite multiple attempts to move the hat out of her system, it was ultimately too much to overcome," it said on Thursday evening, local time. "The team performed necessary supportive care today in an attempt to save her, but it was not successful and she did not recover. "We know everyone in the community will be crushed by this news, as we all are." Before she died, veterinarians had been keeping Fiona hydrated, giving her treats and monitoring her every move, the zoo said. Loading... They even borrowed a vibration plate from a horse farm, encouraging her to stand on it several times a day in the hopes that the shaking would help move things along through her digestive tract. Surgery was not an option given Fiona's size, the zoo said. In a joint post with US Vice-President JD Vance on Instagram, second lady Usha Vance shared a photo of one of their children face-to-face with Fiona through a glass wall of her enclosure. The family has a home in Cincinnati. Cincinnati Mayor Aftab Pureval described Fiona as "a symbol of perseverance and joy in Cincinnati". "She brought smiles to so many faces, from kids to parents to visitors from around the world," he said on X. Fiona was born six weeks premature in January 2017 weighing only 13 kilograms, less than half a normal birth weight. She was unable to stand and faced long survival odds. She was named after the Shrek character. Fans from around the world watched every development online, as the zoo recorded daily updates on her feeding, her growth and her activities. She even inspired a children's book series. Her story marked an uplifting turn for the Cincinnati Zoo following months of backlash over the shooting of Harambe, the gorilla who became a pop culture phenomenon after he was killed after a child got into his enclosure. The zoo's hippo family expanded in 2022 with the birth of Fiona's baby brother, Fritz. Fiona's father, Henry, was euthanised months after her birth as his health badly declined. He had lived 36 years, which was slightly beyond the average life expectancy for a Nile hippopotamus in captivity. **ABC/wires**
